The savings made by hyperscale centres can be seen in their power usage efficiency
(PUE), defined as the total energy needed for everything, including lights and cooling, divided by the energy used for computing (a PUE of 1.0 would be a perfect score).
Conventional data centres typically have a PUE of about 2.0; for hyperscale facilities, that’s been whittled down to about 1.2
. Google, for one, boasts a PUE of 1.12 on average for all its centres.
